title: BookGraph
description: Standardized schema for a single book's explorable knowledge graph. Node and edge vocabulary is organized around Mortimer Adler's four levels of reading (How to Read a Book): Elementary (raw content), Inspectional (overview/skim), Analytical (deep single-book structure), Syntopical (cross-book synthesis — see master-graph.schema.json, which composes this file's output across books).

schemaVersion.description: Bump on breaking changes to node/edge shape.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. 'mans-search-for-meaning'. Used as the node-id namespace prefix.

copyrightStatus.description: Legal review flag. 'unreviewed' should block publishing to a paid tier.

curator.description: Who authored/reviewed this graph (person, or 'llm-draft' pending human review).

sourceEditions.description: Which edition/translation the page/chapter refs below point to.

readingLevel.description: Which Adler level this node primarily serves. Drives progressive disclosure: inspectional-only view shows themes; analytical view expands to concept/quote/example; syntopical nodes only ever appear in the master graph, never a single-book view.

type.description: book: single root node. theme: top-level branch (Adler-inspectional unit, e.g. a principle/chapter cluster). topic: sub-idea under a theme. concept: fine-grained idea (analytical depth). quote: verbatim text with citation. example: illustrative anecdote/case. vocabulary: a term this book uses in a load-bearing way (feeds syntopical vocabulary-building).

content.description: Body text: paraphrase for concept/topic, verbatim text for quote.

vocabularyTerm.description: For type=vocabulary: the canonical term (e.g. 'logotherapy', 'preparation'). Used by the master graph to detect shared/overlapping vocabulary across books.

parentId.description: Id of the containing node (book->theme->topic->concept hierarchy). Root 'book' node omits this.

position.description: Optional pre-computed layout hint; renderer may ignore and force-layout instead.

relation.description: contains: hierarchy edge (book->theme->topic->concept), rendered as solid tree lines. relates_to: same-book thematic association (dotted, per the Frankl PR's cross-link arrows). supports/conflicts_with: the author's own stated agreement/tension between two ideas *within this book*. answers_question / shares_vocabulary_with: reserved for use by the master graph when composing multiple BookGraphs; a single-book graph should rarely need them.

label.description: Optional short gloss on the relation, e.g. 'both trace back to freedom of will'.
